newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Post Office losses slammed.
newsitem.headline: S.African Post Office losses slammed.

text.p: The South African parliamentary finance committee on Monday slammed government's failure to stem losses in the Post Office.
State Expenditure director-general Hannes Smit confirmed that the Post Office had been due to turn around a deficit of 590.4 million rand in 1992/93 to a surplus of 10.6 million rand in 1996/97.
But in 1996/97 the Post Office has a deficit of 572 million rand.

Posts and Telecommunications director-general Andile Ngcaba said a special team had now been appointed to examine the restructuring of the Post Office, which could include franchising out certain operations.

African National Congress legislator Barbara Hogan said that in terms of the agreement reached when the Post Office was hived off as a separate company from state telecommunications group, Telkom, it was supposed to gradually reduce its losses.

"I do not know how long we can sustain this kind of situation where we allow parastatals or what-ever to just call upon us for guarantees to back their losses without identifying the problem and taking corrective action immediately," Hogan said.
"Why has the department been so slow to respond to a major crisis in financing?" she asked
Ngcaba assured the committee that this was "one matter we are looking at very seriously" and would be addressed before the end of the year.
